meta.title: LlamaIndex Agents and Workflows
meta.thesis: LlamaIndex Agents and Workflows is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A LlamaIndex workflow searches product docs, checks sources, and escalates low-confidence answers. By the end, they should be able to build or review LlamaIndex agent workflow with retrieval and citation nodes, measure source-backed answers on known support issues, and catch the failure where the workflow retrieves good nodes but drops source metadata before generation.

mentalMap.caption: Teach LlamaIndex agents and workflows as data-centric RAG plus tools, query engines, and event-driven multi-step processes.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: LlamaIndex is the right framework lesson when data preparation and retrieval quality are central to the agent’s work.

modules.title: Data preparation is the center of gravity
modules.sub: Agents work best when the indexed data layer is trustworthy.
modules.summary: The agent inherits the quality of the index.
objectives: Connect documents, nodes, indexes, and query engines to agents.

blocks.title: LlamaIndex agents stand on query engines

spans.text: Problem anchor: a research assistant answers over product manuals, policy PDFs, and support tickets. The hard part is loading, parsing, indexing, retrieving, and citing data. LlamaIndex gives those steps first-class objects.
An agent can call query engines as tools, but the query engine must already retrieve useful source nodes. Tool orchestration cannot fix bad parsing.
Inspect source nodes before judging the agent answer.

blocks.analogy: The agent is the tour guide; the index is the map.

spans.text: One query engine covers product manuals and another covers release notes. The agent chooses which engine to query, then synthesizes an answer with source nodes.
If release note parsing drops version headings, the agent cannot recover that provenance later.

items.text: Load and parse documents into nodes.

blocks.title: Center of gravity
blocks.prompt: What should be fixed first if a LlamaIndex agent cites weak snippets?

options.text: The data parsing, node metadata, index, or retriever behind the query engine.

blocks.explanation: Retrieval quality comes before agent orchestration.

modules.title: Query engines become tools
modules.sub: Agents can call data interfaces and ordinary functions.
modules.summary: LlamaIndex agents can combine data tools with action tools.
objectives: Write tool names and descriptions that guide model choice.
Separate read tools from side-effect tools.

blocks.title: A query engine is a safe read tool when scoped well

spans.text: A query engine tool should have a narrow name, description, and source scope: search_product_manual, search_release_notes, or search_policy. This helps the model choose the right evidence source.
Ordinary functions can also be tools, such as calculators or ticket lookups. Side-effecting tools need the same validation and approval discipline as any agent framework.
Tool descriptions should mention what the tool cannot answer.

blocks.analogy: Each query engine is a reference desk with a clearly labeled section.

cells.text: Ask indexed data for cited evidence.
Bad nodes lead to weak citations.
One broad tool for every corpus.

blocks.title: Tool boundary
blocks.prompt: Why expose release notes and manuals as separate tools?

options.text: Separate tools remove the need for metadata.
The model can choose the evidence source more reliably and traces are clearer.

blocks.explanation: Narrow tools improve routing and evaluation.

modules.title: Workflows coordinate multi-step data tasks
modules.sub: LlamaIndex workflows combine agents, connectors, and tool calls.
objectives: Describe LlamaIndex workflows at a practical level.
Choose workflow steps for extraction or review.
Avoid hiding data errors inside agents.

blocks.title: Workflows make data processes explicit

spans.text: A document assistant may need to ingest a file, extract entities, query related notes, ask an agent to draft, and run a faithfulness check. A workflow gives that process named steps.
Use workflows when ordering, branching, or review matters. Use a simple query engine when the task is direct Q&A.
If a step has a deterministic validator, keep it as code rather than asking the agent to self-certify.

blocks.analogy: A workflow is a checklist the agent cannot skip.

spans.text: A support-ticket workflow extracts product/version, queries manuals and release notes, drafts a response, then verifies that cited source nodes support every claim.
Unsupported claims route to revision or refusal.

blocks.title: Workflow fit
blocks.prompt: When should you use a LlamaIndex workflow instead of only a query engine?

options.text: When the process has ordered steps such as extraction, multiple queries, verification, or action.
When you want to hide all traces.

modules.title: Code a query-engine-backed agent
modules.sub: The useful example prints source nodes.
modules.summary: A LlamaIndex agent should expose the evidence path.
objectives: Build query engine and tool shape.
Predict which tool answers a question.
Inspect source nodes or tool outputs.

spans.text: A minimal example should load documents, create an index, expose the query engine, and show the source nodes behind the response. The agent layer is only useful when evidence remains visible.
Spaced recall: from RAG faithfulness, final claims must map to retrieved context. LlamaIndex source nodes are the review surface.
Add one question the index cannot answer and verify refusal.

blocks.title: LlamaIndex query engine as an agent tool
blocks.code:
from llama_index.core import Document, VectorStoreIndex

manuals = [Document(text="Refund exceptions for enterprise plans require finance approval.", metadata={"source": "billing.md"})]
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(manuals)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine(similarity_top_k=2)

def search_billing_policy(question: str) -> str:
    response = query_engine.query(question)
    sources = [n.metadata.get("source") for n in response.source_nodes]
    return f"{response}
Sources: {sources}"

print(search_billing_policy("Who approves enterprise refund exceptions?"))
blocks.explanation: The function wraps a query engine and returns sources with the answer. A full FunctionAgent would register this as a tool.

predictThenReveal.prompt: Before reading the answer, predict which source should appear.
predictThenReveal.answer: `billing.md` should appear because the document contains the finance-approval fact.

blocks.title: Source node review
blocks.prompt: What should you inspect if the agent answer is wrong?

options.text: The query engine’s retrieved source nodes and metadata.

blocks.explanation: The data layer is the likely failure surface.

modules.title: Evaluate retrieval before agent skill
modules.sub: An agent cannot reason from evidence it never receives.
modules.summary: Data eval is the release gate.
objectives: Test tool selection and no-answer cases.

blocks.title: The agent is downstream of retrieval

spans.text: Evaluation should record question, expected source nodes, retrieved nodes, final answer, and claim support. Tool selection matters too: the model should choose manuals for policy questions and release notes for version questions.
Failure modes include bad parsing, wrong index, weak tool descriptions, overbroad query engines, missing refusal behavior, and source nodes that do not support claims.
Do not add more agents until direct query-engine eval passes.

blocks.title: Verify AI output from LlamaIndex agents

spans.text: Review answer, selected tool, and source nodes.

items.text: The selected query engine matches the question and corpus.
Source nodes include the facts used in the answer.
The agent refuses or asks when evidence is absent.
Workflow validators route unsupported claims to revision or refusal.

blocks.title: LlamaIndex gate
blocks.prompt: What should block adding a multi-step agent workflow?

options.text: The query engine prints source nodes.
The underlying query engine fails direct retrieval and faithfulness checks.

blocks.explanation: Reliable data retrieval is the foundation.

questions.q: Is the agent mainly orchestrating tools around private or structured data indexes?
questions.why: LlamaIndex shines when readers, nodes, indexes, retrievers, and query engines dominate behavior.
questions.rot: Use LlamaIndex when data objects and retrieval quality are the heart of the agent; use graph frameworks when control flow dominates.
